assertions.name: n_lambda_with_a_constant_sign
assertions.source: sympy exact; a constant eps_lambda would make this nonzero

description: The V_lambda <-> V_{lambda'} intertwiner is the sign-twisted map sigma -> -sigma^{-1}, not the bar involution. The character identity of eigenbasis-structural-lemmas item 2 holds, but its sign is (-1)^L in the word length, not a per-channel eps_lambda.

parameters.exact: sympy over QQ(q); no substrate pin used

interpretation.the_intertwiner: sigma_i -> -sigma_i^{-1} (the Iwahori-Matsumoto-type sign twist) is an algebra automorphism that swaps the eigenvalues q <-> -q^{-1} and carries V_lambda to V_{lambda'}. The bar involution does not: it fixes each eigenchannel. The two differ by exactly the sign.
interpretation.the_identity_holds: chi_lambda(q^{-1}) = eps * chi_{lambda'}(q) is true on every braid word tested in H_2 and H_3, so the block's conclusion -- and the matter/antimatter reading built on it -- stands.
interpretation.but_the_sign_is_not_per_channel: eps = (-1)^L in the word length L, not a constant eps_lambda attached to the partition. For every lambda tested, including the self-conjugate (2,1), eps takes both values as L varies. Writing eps_lambda claims a per-channel invariant that does not exist.
interpretation.honest_restatement: chi_lambda(-q^{-1}) = chi_{lambda'}(q), unsigned. Combined with item 1's parity chi(-q) = (-1)^L chi(q) this reproduces the signed form, and it says plainly what the operation is: the eigenvalue swap q -> -q^{-1}.

caveats: Verified on H_2 and H_3 over braid words of length <= 6 (length <= 4 for the unsigned form). Not a proof for general n; the Hoefsmit 2-dimensional (2,1) rep is the only multi-dimensional channel exercised.

Positive braid words only (no sigma_i^{-1} letters). The parity bookkeeping (-1)^L is stated for L = word length in that setting; for words with negative letters L should be read as the exponent sum, which is not tested here.
